25 A train that is moving in a straight line along a railway track has a whistle that continuously emits
sound of frequency f.
A woman standing by the side of the track hears sound of frequency 0.85f.
The speed of sound in the air is 340 m s–1.
What is the velocity of the train?
A
51 m s–1 away from the woman
B
51 m s–1 towards the woman
C
60 m s–1 away from the woman
D
60 m s–1 towards the woman

hints: Notice the heard frequency $0.85f$ is lower than the emitted frequency $f$ with sound speed $340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ - decide whether a lower pitch means the train is approaching or receding.
Recall how source motion changes observed wavelength: a receding train stretches each wavelength to $\lambda' = (v+v_s)/f$, so observed frequency is $f_o = v/\lambda'$.
Set $0.85f = f \times 340/(340+v_s)$, cancel $f$, and solve for $v_s$ - check why this gives a larger value than $0.15 \times 340$.
walkthrough: Observed frequency $0.85f$ is less than source frequency $f$. Lower frequency means longer observed wavelength, so the source must be moving away from the stationary woman.
For a source receding at speed $v_s$ in sound speed $v$, each period the source moves further away, so $\lambda_o = (v+v_s)/f$ and $f_o = v/\lambda_o = f \times v/(v+v_s)$.
Substitute $f_o = 0.85f$ and $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$: $0.85f = f \times 340/(340+v_s)$. Cancel $f$ to get $0.85 = 340/(340+v_s)$.
Combine speed $60 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with the receding direction identified in step 1. This is option C.

A.explanation: Direction away is correct because $0.85f < f$, but $51 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ comes from $0.15 \times 340$, which ignores the changed denominator in the Doppler equation.

B.explanation: Moving towards the woman would compress wavefronts and give observed frequency greater than $f$, not $0.85f$, and $51 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is also the wrong magnitude.

C.explanation: Receding source gives $0.85f = f \times 340/(340+v_s)$, so $340+v_s = 400$ and $v_s = 60 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ away from the woman.

D.explanation: $60 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is the correct speed magnitude, but motion towards the woman would raise the observed frequency above $f$ rather than lower it to $0.85f$.
